Subject: ACME POC: evaluation plan & success criteria

Hi Karen / Tom,

Thanks again for the demo today — really helpful to see the ACME search assistant flows. Per our call I put together a one-page POC success criteria and a draft evaluation plan (attached) so we can align on scope and measurement. High-level proposal: 

- Goal: Validate Redwood inference economics and quality on ACME search assistant use case
- Duration: 4 weeks (3 week active eval + 1 week buffer)
- Success criteria:
  1) Mean latency < 250ms (p50), p95 < 800ms for the expected traffic pattern
  2) Semantic relevance: top-3 end-user satisfaction >= 85% (measured via blind eval)
  3) Cost target: <= $0.015 per query (token-normalized)
  4) Error rate < 1% (timeouts / 500s)

Owners:
- Redwood: Marissa (program), Monica (technical), Dev (infra)
- ACME: Karen (product), Tom (procurement)

Next steps: 
1) Align on offline eval methodology vs online shadow — see the attached rubric (acme-poc-eval-rubric.xlsx)
2) Kickoff call next week to finalize DS access & test dataset
3) Procurement milestone: target signed SOW by end of March

Links & attachments:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=acme-poc-eval-plan
- Attach: acme-poc-success-criteria.pdf, acme-poc-eval-rubric.xlsx

If helpful I can walk through the rubric live — happy to slot 30 minutes on your calendar.

Best,
Marissa

On Mon, Feb 23, 2026 at 9:04 AM Karen Liu <karen.liu@acme.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear plan. A couple of clarifying questions before we lock dates: 
> 
> 1) For the "blind eval" relevance metric, can you confirm the process? Do ACME reviewers see anonymized responses mixed with baselines? Who runs the labeling and how are instructions packaged?
> 2) Some of our search logs include PII. For the POC we'd prefer to run against an isolated environment. Is Redwood's Private deployment an option for the POC? If so, can you send over SOC2 evidence and a rough SOW estimate so I can start procurement conversations.

Thanks Karen — quick answers and a proposed approach below.

Blind / offline eval (recommended first step):
- Redwood provides an anonymized sample of model responses and baseline responses. Human raters (either ACME or a mutually agreed third-party) see prompts with randomized response sets (no model labels). Raters assign a 1-5 relevance score and select the best response for pass/fail.
- Primary metric: Mean relevance score and % of responses where ACME's preferred answer is in the top-3. We map the 1-5 scores to an 85% pass threshold in the rubric (attached).

Online shadow (recommended to validate infra & signal drift):
- Run a 1-week shadow at ~1-3% of traffic to measure latency, error modes, and end-to-end degradations without impacting users. This validates p95/p99 under real load.

Proposed hybrid timeline: start with the 3-week offline eval + parallel infra setup, then a 1-week 2% online shadow in week 3 to validate ops. That gives concrete quality numbers before we scale.

Security & Private deployment: 
- Private deployment is available for POCs; we'll need a short onboarding checklist (networking, keys, dataset access). I'm attaching a SOC2 summary and our standard SOW template to help procurement.

Owners (proposed):
- Redwood: Marissa (program lead), Monica (technical lead / onboarding), Dev (infra / private deploy), Rishi (commercial / SOW)
- ACME: Karen (product lead), Tom (procurement)

Next steps (commercial & technical):
1) ACME confirms whether ACME or Redwood will run human labeling for the offline eval (impacts timing)
2) Redwood shares SOC2 summary + SOW (attached)
3) Kickoff meeting to finalize dataset, test harness, and access schedule

Attachments: acme-poc-eval-rubric.xlsx, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, acme-sow-template.docx

I'll take point on the commercial bits — Marissa / Monica / Dev, can we confirm availability for a kickoff on 3/1 and owners for the first onboarding tasks?

Thanks,
